title: Sherpa Tensing — Camp Six: Past Continuous (A2) | Forbes English
description: Camp three struck the tent and walked away. Camp six goes back and stands inside the day itself — the rain that was already falling, the argument that was…

hero.h1: The weather you were already in
hero.lede: Camp three struck the tent and walked away. Camp six goes back and stands inside the day itself — the rain that was already falling, the argument that was already running, the thing that was going on when something else cut across it.

sections.label: Basecamp briefing
sections.title: When to use it
sections.lead: Start here: the past continuous is the background tense. Its first job is context — what was already going on, and what you were in the middle of — and everything else it does follows from that.

cards.head: The background everything else happens in
cards.body: This is what the tense is for. It paints the scene — the weather, the room, the mood — and the story is then told on top of it in camp three.
cards.ex: "It was raining. Nobody was speaking. The fire was burning low."

cards.head: In the middle of an action in progress
cards.body: You are standing inside the action, not looking back at it. It had already started, and it had not yet finished.

cards.head: The action that got interrupted
cards.body: The background was already running when a shorter, finished action cut across it.
cards.ex: "I was driving home when the call came."

cards.head: Two things at once
cards.body: Both were in progress side by side, usually joined by while.

cards.head: A temporary past situation
cards.body: True for a stretch of time, and not any more.
cards.ex: "That year we were living above the bakery."

cards.head: Softening what you want
cards.body: The past continuous makes a request sound less blunt.
cards.ex: "I was wondering whether you had a moment."

charts.head: Conjugation chart
charts.note: Only be changes, and it changes exactly as it does in camp three — was for I, he, she and it; were for the rest. The -ing form never moves.

charts.head: The verbs that refuse the -ing
charts.note: State verbs describe a condition rather than an activity, and English does not put a condition in the continuous. These take the past simple even when everything around them is continuous.

charts.head: Three mistakes worth naming
charts.note: Almost every error with this tense is one of these three.

head: Not this
This
Why
rows: State verbs do not take the continuous.
While I was walking, it was starting to rain.
While I was walking, it started to rain.
The thing that cuts in is short and finished: past simple.

charts.note: Camp three and camp six describe the same night. The difference is whether you are standing inside the action or looking back at it as one finished event.

head: Question
Past continuous
Past simple
rows:
Does the interrupting.
"I was reading when the lights went out."

Always.
"She stood up, paid and left."

charts.example: The reliable test: while takes the long action, when takes the short one. "While I was cooking, the phone rang" and "When the phone rang, I was cooking" are the same night told from opposite ends.

sections.label: Trail markers
sections.title: Signal words

signals.head: The long action
items: all morning / all day / all night

sections.example: If a sentence has both, they almost always split the same way: while + was/were doing, when + past simple.

sections.title: The long action and the short one

The brown bar dropping into it is camp three: one short, finished action, cutting in. Click either to name it and see it in a sentence.

panels.head: Past continuous — the long action
items: I was driving home in the dark.
That year we were living above the bakery.

quiz.prompt: I _____ home when the call came. (drive)
quiz.hint: The long action that got interrupted.
quiz.explain: The action already running takes the past continuous: was driving. The short thing that cut in — the call — takes the past simple.

quiz.hint: "While" almost always takes the long action.
quiz.explain: While introduces the background action, so it takes the past continuous: while she was cooking.

quiz.prompt: When the lights went out, we _____ dinner. (have)
quiz.hint: Which half is the background here?
quiz.explain: The dinner was already in progress when the lights went out, so it takes the past continuous with the plural were.

quiz.prompt: They _____ ready when the taxi arrived. (not / be)
quiz.hint: Careful — be is a state verb.
quiz.explain: Be describes a state, so it stays in the past simple: they weren't ready. "Weren't being ready" is not English.

quiz.prompt: I _____ the answer at the time. (know)
quiz.explain: Know is a state verb and refuses the continuous. Past simple: I knew.

quiz.hint: Question order for the past continuous.
quiz.explain: Questions invert be: Were you sleeping? You is plural in form, so it takes were.

quiz.prompt: He _____ his keys that summer. (always / lose)
quiz.hint: A complaint, not a neutral fact.
quiz.explain: Always + the past continuous carries irritation: he was always losing his keys. Always lost would just be a habit.

quiz.prompt: She stood up, _____ the bill and left. (pay)
quiz.explain: A sequence of completed actions stays in the past simple throughout. The past continuous never tells a sequence.

quiz.prompt: At eight o'clock last night I _____ on a train. (sit)
quiz.hint: A clock time in the past, mid-action.
quiz.explain: A precise past moment with the action already under way takes the past continuous: I was sitting.

quiz.prompt: I _____ whether you had a moment. (wonder)
quiz.explain: The past continuous makes a request less blunt: I was wondering whether… It is politeness, not past time.

quiz.prompt: While we _____ , they _____ the whole flat. (talk / repaint)
quiz.hint: Two long actions at the same time.
quiz.explain: Two actions running side by side both take the past continuous, joined by while.

quiz.prompt: The car _____ when I turned the key. (not / start)
quiz.explain: One completed attempt at a moment in the past is the past simple: it didn't start.

quiz.prompt: It _____ hard, so we stayed in. (rain)
quiz.explain: Weather setting the scene takes the past continuous: it was raining. "It rained" would report the whole day as one finished event.

quiz.hint: Asking about a moment, not a whole night.
quiz.explain: Asking what was in progress at a precise past time takes the past continuous: What were you doing?

results: Clean run. You can hear which action is the background and which one cuts in.
Solid progress. Worth a look back at camp three before camp seven.
Good first attempt. The while/when fork is the part to read again.
